pairs.why: B shows the real card's three-quarter tilt, with the thick side wall and the keys' faces both visible. A is nearly top-down and flat, so it reads as a thin slab.
B turns the chest to show its front and one side, and the camera is above enough to see into the open lid and onto the sand. That matches the real card. A is closer to frontal and reads flatter.

A has the real cards' higher camera, with a visible top face and a wide floor plane under a graphic patterned backdrop. B has a thin top face and a soft photographic background, which the real cards don't have.
A turns the pack to a three-quarter view with the side pocket and strap visible and the top of the bedroll showing, as on the real card. B is mostly frontal and flatter.
A matches the real card's high view with strong foreshortening of the fins, and the foot pockets show their openings. B's fins are longer and flatter, and its pockets sit lower.
A is a front three-quarter view with a layered background, like the real bus and coaster. B is more side-on with weaker depth. A's perspective is slightly strong, so confidence is low.
A is a wall-mounted clock with the rim's thickness and a drop shadow on the backdrop, like the real card. B stands on a floor with a horizon band, which is a different ground and view setup.
